title: Rhythm instruments of the Indians
summary: The Wild Magnolias are heard; Cahn explains tambourine and cowbell, with few drums since the men march all day.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: When did you... How does... You've... We'll listen to some... You know, in between when we're talking, we'll try to listen to some music, which the Indians have done. What we just heard was the Wild Magnolias. Now, you... It said... Now, obviously, the purest of the Indians, when you hear the Indians, you don't hear them with musical instruments. You hear them with, basically, rhythm instruments, right?

Yes. They have the tambourine and the cowbell. The cowbell. That's it, more or less. They have introduced... A couple of tribes have introduced either a bass drum or a type of bongo. Right. Or march bongo. But you have to realize that on Mardi Gras Day, these fellas march from 6 or 7 in the morning until midnight. And you just can't carry an amplified bass around.
